track.line: Aldactone, 1960; heart, BP, edema. Acne off-label

what.text: Spironolactone is an aldosterone antagonist, a medicine taken by mouth. It blocks aldosterone at the kidney, so the body passes more salt and water while keeping potassium. That is how it works as a diuretic and blood-pressure medicine.

It also binds the androgen (male hormone) receptor, and the label describes anti-androgenic effects. The FASCE trial authors say it targets the androgen receptor of the skin's oil glands and is prescribed off-label for acne in adult women.

src.label: Dréno et al. (FASCE), Acta Derm Venereol, 2024

what.text: Spironolactone is in the Adonis treatment library as a compounded prescription product. Its form is not on file.
Using spironolactone for acne is off-label. No FDA-approved spironolactone label lists acne.

research.text: Two randomized trials have tested spironolactone for acne, and both enrolled only women: SAFA in England and Wales (410 women, against placebo) and FASCE in France (133 women, against doxycycline). Neither tells us how it works or how safe it is in men.
Each study is listed below as it was run.

research.meta: England and Wales · 2019 to 2021 · Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
research.title: SAFA: spironolactone vs placebo for acne in women

facts.v: pragmatic, multicenter, Phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled; topical treatment allowed
410 women aged 18 or over with facial acne for at least six months (201 spironolactone, 209 placebo); 342 in the main analysis. Mean age 29
50 mg a day to week 6, then 100 mg a day to week 24, or matching placebo
acne quality-of-life symptom score at week 12 (main measure); week 24; self-rated and investigator-rated improvement; side effects

research.found: At week 12 the quality-of-life score was 1.27 points better on spironolactone (on a 0 to 30 scale), and 3.45 points better at week 24. Investigator-rated success at week 12 was 19% vs 6%. Headaches were more common on spironolactone (20% vs 12%). No serious adverse reactions were reported.

research.title: FASCE: spironolactone vs doxycycline in women with acne

facts.v: multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel groups; both arms also used benzoyl peroxide
spironolactone for 6 months, vs doxycycline for 3 months then placebo for 3 months
treatment success on the AFAST acne score at months 4 and 6

research.found: Success at 6 months was significantly higher with spironolactone (P = 0.007). The authors describe spironolactone as prescribed off-label for adult female acne.

src.label: Dréno et al. (FASCE), Acta Derm Venereol, 2024

items.text: In long-term feeding studies in rats, spironolactone caused tumors, including benign thyroid and testicular tumors, liver tumors in males, and thyroid cancers in both sexes.
In rats, exposure late in pregnancy feminized male fetuses. The label advises avoiding it in pregnancy because of the risk to a male fetus.

us.text: Spironolactone is FDA approved as Aldactone, first approved on January 21, 1960, for heart failure, high blood pressure, edema and primary hyperaldosteronism. Acne is not an approved use; using it for acne is off-label. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: heart failure (NYHA class III to IV with reduced ejection fraction); add-on treatment of high blood pressure; edema from liver cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome; and primary hyperaldosteronism.
off-label. Acne is not among the label's indications.

world.lead: Spironolactone is an approved prescription medicine in the US, across the EU (including one centrally authorised liquid, Qaialdo) and in Northern Ireland, for heart, blood-pressure and fluid conditions. None of the records checked lists acne. It is banned in sport at all times as a diuretic.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Spironolactone is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) under class S5, diuretics and masking agents, on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List, where it is named. All S5 substances are Specified Substances. An athlete would need a therapeutic use exemption to use it.

side.text: In men, spironolactone can cause breast growth (gynecomastia), lower libido and trouble getting or keeping an erection. It can also raise blood potassium to dangerous levels. These are on the FDA label.

items.text: the label says Aldactone can cause gynecomastia and that it is the most common side effect. In the RALES heart-failure trial, about 9% of men on a mean 26 mg a day developed it. The risk rises with dose; it can start within 1 to 2 months or after more than a year, and is usually reversible.
decreased libido and inability to achieve or maintain an erection are listed. In women: irregular or absent periods, bleeding after menopause, and breast and nipple pain.

Aldactone can cause hyperkalemia. The risk is higher with kidney problems, potassium supplements, salt substitutes, or drugs such as ACE inhibitors and ARBs. The label calls for a potassium check within 1 week of starting and regularly after. It must not be used by people who already have high potassium.
too much fluid loss can cause dehydration, low blood pressure and worsening kidney function.
low sodium, low magnesium, low calcium, high blood sugar and high uric acid (rarely gout).
Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS, low white cells (including agranulocytosis), low platelets, and a very few cases of liver injury, one fatal.
it raises lithium levels, and it can raise PSA in men taking abiraterone for prostate cancer; that combination is not recommended.
in SAFA, headaches were more common on spironolactone than placebo (20% vs 12%); no serious adverse reactions were reported.

unconfirmed: The form of spironolactone Adonis carries is not on file (BELUGA-FORMS.md), so no form is described.

surprises: Spironolactone is widely prescribed for acne, but no regulator record checked (FDA's Aldactone label, EMA's Qaialdo record) lists acne as an approved use; it is off-label everywhere checked.
It is often thought of as a skin or hormone medicine, but WADA lists it by name as a diuretic and masking agent (S5), prohibited at all times.
The acne trials behind its popularity enrolled only women; in men the label's most common side effect is breast growth, with lower libido and erection problems also listed.
